top_three.title: US data brokers are selling half a billion dollars in RL training environments to Chinese AI labs
top_three.title_en: US data brokers are selling half a billion dollars in RL training environments to Chinese AI labs
top_three.author: THE DECODER
top_three.article_content:
American data brokers sell so-called RL environments to Chinese AI labs, helping them save compute during model development. A ChinaTalk investigation identifies at least nine companies involved.

American data firms like Mercor, Surge AI, AfterQuery, and Turing are selling roughly half a billion dollars' worth of training data to Chinese AI labs, according to an investigation by ChinaTalk. Some of that data takes the form of reinforcement learning environments, which are simulated worlds where AI models are trained on specific tasks like coding, financial analysis, or office work.

Chinese labs deliberately buy the same products previously sold to Anthropic or OpenAI, the report says. That way, they already know the data works and can skip costly in-house development and wasted training runs. Because Chinese chips suffer from acute memory bottlenecks, those savings are particularly valuable for labs there.

There is also the issue of distillation. Chinese labs use powerful US models like GPT or Claude as "teachers," using their outputs as training examples. Combined with purchased RL environments, this creates a two-pronged advantage that lets Chinese labs close the gap with less compute of their own.

The authors identified at least nine US data firms selling to Chinese customers. AfterQuery reportedly draws a significant share of its annual recurring revenue from Chinese customers. ChinaTalk points to Forbes reports of about $100 million in ARR but could not independently verify the sales.

Surge AI openly advertises on its website that its products are "built by the same experts behind our frontier-lab work." The deals also run through offshore structures. ByteDance maintains procurement offices in Singapore and San Jose.

These business relationships came to light through a combination of anonymous sources and sloppy operational security among subcontractors, according to ChinaTalk. The US data firms outsource much of the actual RL environment creation and data curation to low-paid workers in developing countries, especially India. Those subcontractors then sometimes post client names on LinkedIn or in résumés, even though they are supposed to use only code names. Export controls barely apply because RL environments remain largely unregulated.

Domains with dual-use potential pose particular risks: Coding environments improve software development but can also sharpen offensive cyber capabilities. Biology environments could improve gene synthesis capabilities and potentially enhance bioweapons-relevant applications. The ChinaTalk authors argue that the Bureau of Industry and Security should subject these dual-use environments to existing export controls.

At the same time, the authors stress that these relationships are not apocalyptic. By piggybacking on US work, Chinese labs still trail their US peers by at least a few months as a structural matter. Sensitive environments in areas like biology, chemistry, cybersecurity, chip design, and investment banking are increasingly being built in-house at American frontier companies, the authors say.

top_three.article_content_zh:
美国数据经纪人向中国人工智能实验室出售所谓的强化学习环境，帮助他们在模型开发过程中节省计算量。 ChinaTalk 的一项调查发现至少有 9 家公司参与其中。

根据 ChinaTalk 的一项调查，Mercor、Surge AI、AfterQuery 和 Turing 等美国数据公司正在向中国人工智能实验室出售价值约 5 亿美元的训练数据。其中一些数据采用强化学习环境的形式，这些环境是模拟世界，人工智能模型在其中接受编码、财务分析或办公室工作等特定任务的训练。

报告称，中国实验室故意购买之前出售给 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 的相同产品。这样，他们就已经知道数据的工作原理，并且可以跳过昂贵的内部开发和浪费的培训运行。由于中国芯片存在严重的内存瓶颈，因此这些节省对于那里的实验室来说特别有价值。

还有蒸馏的问题。中国实验室使用 GPT 或 Claude 等强大的美国模型作为“老师”，使用它们的输出作为训练示例。与购买的强化学习环境相结合，这创造了一个双管齐下的优势，让中国实验室可以用更少的计算来缩小差距。

作者确定了至少九家向中国客户销售产品的美国数据公司。据报道，AfterQuery 的年度经常性收入中有很大一部分来自中国客户。 ChinaTalk 指出《福布斯》报道称 ARR 约为 1 亿美元，但无法独立核实销售额。

Surge AI 在其网站上公开宣传其产品“由我们前沿实验室工作背后的同一位专家打造”。这些交易还通过离岸结构进行。字节跳动在新加坡和圣何塞设有采购办事处。

据 ChinaTalk 报道，这些业务关系是通过匿名消息来源和分包商之间草率的运营安全的结合而曝光的。美国数据公司将大部分实际的强化学习环境创建和数据管理外包给发展中国家（尤其是印度）的低薪工人。这些分包商有时会在 LinkedIn 或简历中发布客户姓名，尽管他们应该只使用代号。出口管制几乎不适用，因为强化学习环境在很大程度上仍然不受监管。

具有双重用途潜力的领域会带来特殊的风险：编码环境可以改善软件开发，但也可以增强进攻性网络能力。生物环境可以提高基因合成能力，并有可能增强生物武器相关的应用。 ChinaTalk 的作者认为，工业和安全局应该将这些双重用途环境置于现有的出口管制之下。

同时，作者强调这些关系并不是世界末日。通过借助美国的研究成果，中国实验室在结构性问题上仍然落后美国同行至少几个月。作者表示，生物、化学、网络安全、芯片设计和投资银行等领域的敏感环境越来越多地在美国前沿公司内部建立。

top_three.title: Adobe’s AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters
top_three.title_en: Adobe’s AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters
top_three.author: The Verge AI
top_three.article_content:
Some of the most impressive tech that Adobe showcases at its annual Max conference each year is the experimental features it’s developing, and the latest of those tools are being announced today: they can transform images into explorable 3D scenes, design AI characters by talking to them, and turn photo editing into a copy/paste process.

The first (and weirdest, in my opinion) is Project Screen Test, which is designed to make AI-generated characters easier to develop and use for video content. Instead of just describing how the character should sound and behave in text prompts, the tool lets you talk to the character and direct them in an audition-like environment. You start by describing some base personality traits, such as “anxious, shy, awkward,” and giving the character a voice, either by selecting a preset, describing how it sounds in a prompt, or uploading sample audio for it to reference.

You can then expand its persona in further detail by conversing with the character as if you’re talking on FaceTime, outlining its backstory, temperament, goals, flaws, fears, movement quirks and more. Once you’re happy, the tool lets you generate animated screen tests with the character by describing an environment or scenario you want to put them in.

[Image: This Personality tab lets you manually adjust any of the traits that were generated for the character by talking to it. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/Screenshot-2026-11-11-085454.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

This is currently a standalone creative exercise, and it’s not clear how (or if) it could feature in any of Adobe’s existing AI video tools. The results provided a more identifiable and consistent personality compared to many soulless animated AI characters I’ve seen, but that’s the entire reason this exists — AI video generation provides far less creative control compared to traditional animation, where every aspect of a character is included with absolute intention.

There’s also Project Sight Span, which reframes photographs and images by turning them into a 3D environment that you can navigate through and reposition. The 3D space generates objects and backgrounds that are outside of the original frame, but feel like a natural part of the image, even if you’re turning to see what’s behind you. While the visuals in the 3D environment are pixelated and ill–defined, the resolution quality is restored when you select your chosen angle.

[Image: This still doesn’t really do Project Sight Span justice, but a video demonstration should take place at the Adobe Max sneaks keynote. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/Screenshot-2026-11-11-085101.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

Sight Span works with any flat image, including photos, paintings, and illustrations, and can preserve and replicate artistic styles. Even repositioned tattoos and facial features in photographs remain surprisingly recognizable and true to the original reference. It’s a bit like a version of Apple’s Spatial Reframing feature on steroids: you can reposition more aggressively and change the shooting point entirely if you want, but it also feels far less deserving of being called a photo afterward.

top_three.article_content_zh:
Adobe 每年在年度 Max 会议上展示的一些最令人印象深刻的技术是其正在开发的实验性功能，而这些工具中的最新功能今天即将发布：它们可以将图像转换为可探索的 3D 场景，通过与 AI 角色对话来设计它们，以及将照片编辑变成复制/粘贴过程。

第一个（在我看来也是最奇怪的）是 Project Screen Test，它旨在使人工智能生成的角色更容易开发和用于视频内容。该工具不仅可以在文本提示中描述角色的声音和行为，还可以让您与角色交谈并在类似试镜的环境中指导他们。首先描述一些基本的性格特征，例如“焦虑、害羞、尴尬”，然后通过选择预设、描述提示中的声音或上传示例音频以供参考，为角色提供声音。

然后，您可以通过与该角色交谈（就像在 FaceTime 上交谈一样）来进一步详细扩展其角色，概述其背景故事、气质、目标、缺陷、恐惧、动作怪癖等。一旦您感到满意，该工具就可以让您通过描述您想要将其放入的环境或场景来生成角色的动画屏幕测试。

目前，这是一项独立的创意活动，尚不清楚它如何（或是否）能够在 Adob​​e 现有的任何 AI 视频工具中发挥作用。与我见过的许多没有灵魂的动画人工智能角色相比，结果提供了更可识别和一致的个性，但这就是它存在的全部原因——与传统动画相比，人工智能视频生成提供的创意控制要少得多，传统动画中角色的每个方面都包含绝对意图。

还有 Project Sight Span，它可以将照片和图像转变为可以导航和重新定位的 3D 环境，从而重新构建照片和图像。 3D 空间生成原始框架之外的对象和背景，但感觉就像图像的自然部分，即使您转身看后面的东西也是如此。虽然 3D 环境中的视觉效果是像素化且不明确的，但当您选择所选角度时，分辨率质量会恢复。

Sight Span 适用于任何平面图像，包括照片、绘画和插图，并且可以保留和复制艺术风格。即使照片中重新定位的纹身和面部特征仍然令人惊讶地可识别，并且与原始参考相符。这有点像苹果空间重构功能的增强版本：如果你愿意，你可以更积极地重新定位并完全改变拍摄点，但它也让人感觉根本不值得被称为照片。

Project Sound Bender 是一项 AI 音频混合功能，可让您自定义音效，就像在色轮周围单击光标一样。它的工作原理是上传视频剪辑，然后在文本提示中描述您想要的音频，例如“冒泡的科幻大锅噪音”。然后，Sound Bender 会生成声音效果并自动将其同步到视频，并提供方形声音画布，让您可以实时调整噪音。画布的每个角落都会自动分配一个相关的人工智能生成的声音，比如密集的汩汩声和爆破的气泡声、隆隆的沸腾岩石声、尖锐的布洛普声和噼啪作响的电火声。您可以在画布上拖动光标来选择最突出的噪音，或使用不同的声音效果自定义每个角落。

Adobe 还展示了 Project Rinse Repeat，它允许您复制编辑内容，然后自动将它们应用到同一张照片中的其他对象或人物。例如，如果您煞费苦心地用喷枪去除一个人身上的痤疮或瑕疵，“冲洗重复”功能会将您的具体更改调整到一组需要类似修饰的其他人身上。它还可用于在营销图形中为产品添加阴影，即使对象具有不同的形状和大小。 Rinse Repeat 是围绕 Photoshop 构建的，您应用于其他主题的编辑仍然完全可编辑，因为该工具使用本机 Photoshop 工具重新创建它们。

这些“先睹为快”是功能的技术预览，最终可能会开发成 Adob​​e Creative Cloud 应用程序或 Firefly 平台的工具，因此不能保证它们会逐渐成为可用功能。然而，几乎所有这些项目都是围绕 Adob​​e 的生成式 AI 开发而构建的，并且鉴于 AI 工具现在在该公司的增长战略中发挥着核心作用，因此至少其中一些实验可能会正式启动。尽管这些人工智能实验既古怪又有趣，但它们也是一个预兆。如果它们足够有用，这意味着人工智能最终可能会取代创意专业人士目前使用的工具和库存库，无论他们对这项技术的感受有多复杂。

linked_tweets.author: CHIIIDEX 💔💔
linked_tweets.content_zh:
经过充分训练的人工智能模型并不意味着它不再需要计算能力。

训练教会模型如何识别模式、理解语言和生成响应。

但每次有人使用该模型时，它仍然需要计算资源来处理请求并产生答案，这称为推理。

想象一下数百万人同时使用 ChatGPT、生成图像、编写代码和运行 AI 代理。每次交互都需要处理能力。

与训练不同，推理是一个持续的过程。当模型发布时它并没有停止。

这就是人工智能公司继续投资数十亿美元建设数据中心和数千个 GPU 的原因。

构建智能模型是一项挑战。拥有足够的计算能力来服务世界是另一回事。
linked_tweets.content_en:
An AI model being fully trained doesn’t mean it stops needing computing power.

Training teaches the model how to recognize patterns, understand language, and generate responses. 

But every time someone uses that model, it still needs computing resources to process the request and produce an answer., This is called inference.

Think about millions of people using ChatGPT simultaneously, generating images, writing code, and running AI agents. Every interaction requires processing power.

Unlike training, inference is an ongoing process. It doesn’t stop when the model is released.

This is why AI companies continue investing billions in data centers and thousands of GPUs.

Building an intelligent model is one challenge. Having enough computing power to serve the world is another.

linked_tweets.author: Effie Kavoura 🔶
linked_tweets.content_zh:
在添加另一个人工智能代理之前，我会问一个问题。

该代理将改进哪些业务决策？

不是它可以自动化多少任务。演示看起来并不那么令人印象深刻。

工作完成后，公司会发生什么变化？
linked_tweets.content_en:
Before adding another AI agent, I'd ask one question.

What business decision will this agent improve?

Not how many tasks it can automate. Not how impressive the demo looks.

What changes for the company when the work is done?

linked_tweets.author: Emmanuel
linked_tweets.content_zh:
让人工智能代理获得资本是一回事。准确定义它可以用这笔资金做什么是另一回事。

这是@meetmotes 架构的重要组成部分。

每个 Motes NFT 都连接到一个专用的智能账户，而所有者则定义管理代理行为的权限和限制。

这在资产托管和自动执行之间形成了明确的分离。

代理人不应该对某人的资金拥有无限的权力。它的行动应该保持在所有者设定的范围内。

对我来说，这是自主金融的一个重要设计考虑因素。

情报很重要，但控制执行也同样重要。

一个 NFT，一个 Agent，有自己的账户和明确的边界
linked_tweets.content_en:
giving an AI Agent access to capital is one thing. Defining exactly what it can do with that capital is another.

That's an important part of the @meetmotes architecture.

Every Motes NFT is connected to a dedicated smart account,while the owner defines the permissions and limits that govern the agent's actions.

This creates a clear separation between asset custody and automated execution.

The agent isn't supposed to have unlimited authority over someone's funds. Its actions are meant to stay within the boundaries established by the owner.

For me, this is a crucial design consideration for autonomous finance.

Intelligence matters,but controlled execution matters just as much.

One NFT, one Agent, with its own account and defined boundaries

linked_tweets.author: nelson
linked_tweets.content_zh:
人工智能代理经济中最有趣的发展之一是代理雇佣其他代理来完成工作。

@termix_ai 最近通过 Montage Studio 在 上展示了这一点。

这是它的工作原理。

您提交视频制作简介。 Montage Studio 将其分解为更小的工作，并聘请专门的代理来处理故事板、视频渲染和音乐。

然后，它协调他们的工作，合并结果并交付完成的视频。

每个作业都经过 TermiX 上的托管。

这表明代理人如何承担更大的任务，外包专门工作并支付其他代理人的贡献。

但这需要的不仅仅是沟通。代理商需要发现服务、商定价格、确保付款、验证交付和处理纠纷。

这就是 TermiX 的代理自主商务协议 (AACP) 的用武之地。

其工作流程将流程整合在一起：

托管→交付→质疑→结算。

借助 TermiX Skills，代理商还可以连接到市场、寻找工作并参与这些交易。

方向很明确：代理商正在超越孤立的任务，转向雇用、协调和支付其他代理商来完成更大的工作。

这就是 TermiX 正在建设的自主经济。

当代理商开始相互开展业务时，可靠的交易基础设施就变得至关重要。

#TermiX #AACP
linked_tweets.content_en:
one of the more interesting developments in the ai agent economy is agents hiring other agents to get work done.

@termix_ai recently showcased this through Montage Studio on https://t.co/9ReKMK2L7m.

here's how it works.

you submit a video production brief. Montage Studio breaks it into smaller jobs and hires specialized agents to handle the storyboard, video rendering and music.

it then coordinates their work, combines the results and delivers the finished video.

each job goes through escrow on TermiX.

this shows how agents can take responsibility for larger tasks, outsource specialized work and pay other agents for their contributions.

but this requires more than communication. agents need to discover services, agree on prices, secure payments, verify delivery and handle disputes.

that's where TermiX's Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP) comes in.

its workflow brings the process together:

escrow → delivery → challenge → settlement.

with TermiX Skills, agents can also connect to the marketplace, find work and participate in these transactions.

the direction is clear: agents are moving beyond isolated tasks towards hiring, coordinating and paying other agents to complete larger jobs.

that's the kind of autonomous economy TermiX is building towards.

when agents start doing business with each other, reliable transaction infrastructure becomes essential.

#TermiX #AACP

linked_tweets.author: Flames
linked_tweets.content_zh:
告诉人工智能代理它不应该做什么与​​使其在技术上无法做到这一点是不同的。

当人工智能代理处理某人的资金时，这种差异很重要。

您可以告诉代理人避免某些资产、设置支出限额或在出现一定损失后停止交易。但如果它仍然拥有执行交易的广泛权限，那么这些指令就只能到此为止。

通过 MOTES (@meetmotes)，所有者可以设置授权并签署权限。在拟议的交易进行之前，智能账户会根据所有者批准的规则对其进行检查。

因此，代理仍然可以分析市场并制定策略，但它必须在这些限制内运作。它不能只是允许自己在批准的清单之外支出更多资金或交易资产。

我认为这是自主金融更好的基础。赋予代理人做出决策的能力是一回事。确保它仅具有所有者授予的权限也同样重要。
linked_tweets.content_en:
telling an AI agent what it shouldn't do is different from making it technically unable to do it.

when an AI agent is handling someone's money, that difference matters.

you can tell an agent to avoid certain assets, set a spending limit or stop trading after a certain loss. but if it still has broad permission to execute transactions, those instructions only go so far.

with MOTES (@meetmotes), the owner sets the mandate and signs the permissions. before a proposed transaction goes through, the smart account checks it against the rules the owner approved.

so the agent can still analyse the market and come up with strategies, but it has to work within those limits. it can't just give itself permission to spend more or trade assets outside the approved list.

i think this is a better foundation for autonomous finance. giving an agent the ability to make decisions is one thing. making sure it only has the authority the owner gave it is just as important.

news.title: Anthropic says AI is eroding Nvidia's CUDA lead, cutting an AMD chip switch from months to three days
news.title_en: Anthropic says AI is eroding Nvidia's CUDA lead, cutting an AMD chip switch from months to three days
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Anthropic claims it has broken free of its Nvidia dependence with a multi-chip strategy. The company says it ported its own AI model, Claude, to AMD GPUs in just three days, with almost no human intervention.

Nvidia's biggest competitive edge is the combination of hardware and software, specifically CUDA, the software ecosystem that locks developers into Nvidia chips. Porting AI models to other chip architectures takes so much effort that many companies won't even try. Anthropic now claims in an investor presentation that it has solved this problem using AI itself.

According to Tom Brown, co-founder and Chief Compute Officer at Anthropic, the company now trains and runs Claude on all four major chip families. Anthropic made an "unconventional bet" on a multi-chip strategy early on, at a time when most of the industry considered the effort not worth it. Each chip needs its own custom software and inference stack, which is expensive and time-consuming. But Anthropic has been investing in this work for years and has since become "incredibly good" at it, Brown says.

The company's most concrete test came with AMD GPUs. Until now, bringing up a new chip platform kept dozens of engineers busy for months. This year, Anthropic used AMD GPUs for the first time and let its own frontier model, Mythos, do the work. According to Anthropic, Claude was running on AMD after just three days, with almost no human intervention. The model ported or wrote nearly 100 percent of the kernels itself.

If these figures are accurate, the software overhead, long considered Nvidia's strongest competitive advantage, would shrink dramatically because of AI. Companies could switch more easily between chip providers and pick the most affordable or readily available option.

In a compute market where supply is tight, a multi-chip approach lets companies focus on the best price-performance ratio, regardless of the vendor. Some chips are better for training, while others are better for inference. And because of its dominance in the AI chip market, Nvidia currently enjoys a margin of more than 70 percent, which is unusually high for hardware.

Anthropic treats compute from different vendors, chip architectures, and locations as one interchangeable pool. The company says it gets more out of every dollar of compute than any other frontier AI lab.

Beyond its multi-chip strategy, Anthropic relies on what it calls compute multipliers, research breakthroughs that squeeze more performance from the same physical computing capacity. According to Anthropic, these multipliers build on one another so that each new breakthrough amplifies the effect of the previous one.

Eventually, Claude should be able to discover such compute multipliers on its own. That would amount to recursive self-improvement, a concept that's intensely debated in AI research but hasn't been proven yet.

Anthropic is also building its own data center capacity through the "Anthropic Direct" program. Instead of buying computing power only as a cloud service, the company leases chips and operates them in purpose-built data centers. The goal is to reduce total cost of ownership.

The figures come from Anthropic's investor presentation and haven't been independently verified. But they show that at least one major AI lab no longer considers Nvidia's CUDA dominance insurmountable and that AI models themselves could become a tool for breaking hardware dependencies.

news.article_content_zh:
Anthropic 声称，它已经通过多芯片战略摆脱了对 Nvidia 的依赖。该公司表示，它在短短三天内就将自己的人工智能模型 Claude 移植到了 AMD GPU 上，几乎没有人工干预。

Nvidia 最大的竞争优势是硬件和软件的结合，特别是 CUDA，这是将开发人员锁定在 Nvidia 芯片上的软件生态系统。将人工智能模型移植到其他芯片架构需要付出巨大的努力，以至于许多公司甚至不会尝试。 Anthropic 现在在投资者演示中声称，它已经利用人工智能本身解决了这个问题。

Anthropic 联合创始人兼首席计算官 Tom Brown 表示，该公司现在在所有四个主要芯片系列上培训和运行 Claude。 Anthropic 很早就在多芯片战略上做出了“非常规的赌注”，当时大多数行业都认为这种努力不值得。每个芯片都需要自己的定制软件和推理堆栈，这是昂贵且耗时的。但布朗说，Anthropic 多年来一直在这项工作上进行投资，并且自此变得“非常擅长”。

该公司最具体的测试是使用 AMD GPU 进行的。到目前为止，推出新的芯片平台让数十名工程师忙了好几个月。今年，Anthropic 首次使用 AMD GPU，并让其自己的前沿模型 Mythos 来完成这项工作。据 Anthropic 称，Claude 仅三天后就在 AMD 上运行，几乎没有人为干预。该模型移植或编写了几乎 100% 的内核本身。

如果这些数字准确的话，长期以来被认为是 Nvidia 最强竞争优势的软件开销将因人工智能而大幅缩减。公司可以更轻松地在芯片供应商之间切换，并选择最实惠或最容易获得的选项。

在供应紧张的计算市场中，多芯片方法可以让公司专注于最佳性价比，而不管供应商是谁。有些芯片更适合训练，而另一些芯片则更适合推理。而由于在AI芯片市场占据主导地位，英伟达目前享有超过70%的利润率，这对于硬件来说是异常高的。

Anthropic 将来自不同供应商、芯片架构和位置的计算视为一个可互换池。该公司表示，与任何其他前沿人工智能实验室相比，它从每一美元的计算中获得的收益都更多。

除了多芯片策略之外，Anthropic 还依赖所谓的计算倍增器，即在相同物理计算能力的情况下获得更多性能的研究突破。根据 Anthropic 的说法，这些乘数是相互叠加的，因此每一项新突破都会放大前一项突破的效果。

最终，克劳德应该能够自己发现这样的计算乘数。这相当于递归的自我完善，这个概念在人工智能研究中引起了激烈的争论，但尚未得到证实。

Anthropic 还通过“Anthropic Direct”计划建设自己的数据中心容量。该公司不只是购买计算能力作为云服务，而是租赁芯片并在专门构建的数据中心中运行它们。目标是降低总拥有成本。

这些数据来自 Anthropic 的投资者介绍，尚未经过独立验证。但他们表明，至少一个主要的人工智能实验室不再认为 Nvidia 的 CUDA 主导地位是不可逾越的，并且人工智能模型本身可以成为打破硬件依赖性的工具。

两家主要 GPU 制造商现在都与 Anthropic 有着深厚的财务联系。 2025 年 11 月，作为与微软 450 亿美元交易的一部分，Nvidia 承诺向 Anthropic 投资最多 100 亿美元。根据 Anthropic 于 2026 年 11 月 10 日向 SEC 提交的 S-1/A 注册声明，英伟达还参与了总额 260 亿美元的有条件私募，其中七家科技公司以 IPO 价格认购股票。

AMD于2026年7月宣布战略投资高达50亿美元；作为回报，Anthropic 计划在 Helios 机架规模系统中部署高达 2 千兆瓦的 AMD Instinct MI455X GPU，第一个千兆瓦阶段将于 2027 年上半年开始。

news.title: An analysis of 42 interviews since 2022: after US chip restrictions, Jensen Huang's public rhetoric became more admiring of China and critical of export rules (J.D. Capelouto/Semafor)
news.title_en: An analysis of 42 interviews since 2022: after US chip restrictions, Jensen Huang's public rhetoric became more admiring of China and critical of export rules (J.D. Capelouto/Semafor)
news.author: Semafor
news.article_content:
Jensen Huang’s public rhetoric on China became more admiring, and his stance on export controls more critical, after the US restricted Nvidia’s made-for-China chip in 2025 — and as he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

A Semafor analysis of 42 podcast interviews with Huang since early 2022 shows how Huang’s argument around global chip policy evolved in a series of long-form, unscripted, and often friendly settings: Huang talked up China’s strengths and cast Beijing as a formidable competitor as he argued more forcefully for a careful balance between protecting US interests and making US technology the backbone of global AI development.

Whether the Nvidia CEO’s position was shaped by his affair with an executive at a Singapore-based data center firm with alleged ties to Beijing is now a matter for the company’s board, which hired Wall Street law firm Wachtell Lipton to investigate, and for Congress, who plan hearings on the matter. But his stance on China and chip controls is freshly in the spotlight.

Semafor identified dozens of exchanges about China across the interviews and used a pair of AI models from Anthropic and OpenAI to score each one on Huang’s stance on export restrictions and how he regarded China.

Before China’s DeepSeek burst onto the global stage and Washington put new limits on Nvidia’s sales to the country in early 2025, Huang spoke on podcasts about export restrictions in a largely neutral tenor, framing them as a matter of compliance, according to our review.

Mentions of China in Huang’s interviews rose roughly sixfold after those 2025 curbs, as the chip CEO argued that the restrictions hurt the US more than China. “If we leave a market altogether, there’s no question somebody else would step in,” he told Michael Milken in May 2025.

In 14 interviews since the 2025 curbs, he talked up China’s AI researchers, open-source models, and manufacturing, often as reasons the US can’t afford to cut the country off, or rejected the idea of treating it as an enemy.

He invoked the “American tech stack” 34 times across eight interviews since July 2025, arguing that the world’s developers should build on US technology. In eight interviews he said that 50% of the world’s AI researchers are Chinese or in China, suggesting the country’s tech talent can’t be ignored.

news.article_content_zh:
在美国于 2025 年限制英伟达为中国制造的芯片之后，黄仁勋对中国的公开言论变得更加钦佩，他对出口管制的立场也变得更加严厉，而且他与一名涉嫌中国间谍的人有染。

Semafor 对 2022 年初以来对黄仁勋的 42 次播客采访进行了分析，显示了黄仁勋关于全球芯片政策的争论是如何在一系列长期、即兴且往往是友好的环境中演变的：黄仁勋大肆宣扬中国的优势，并将北京视为一个强大的竞争对手，同时他更有力地主张在保护美国利益和让美国技术成为全球人工智能发展支柱之间保持谨慎的平衡。

这位英伟达首席执行官的职位是否受到他与一家新加坡数据中心公司高管的风流韵事的影响，该公司据称与北京有联系，现在是该公司董事会和国会的问题，董事会聘请了华尔街律师事务所 Wachtell Lipton 进行调查，国会则计划就此事举行听证会。但他对中国和芯片控制的立场最近成为人们关注的焦点。

Semafor 在采访中识别了数十条有关中国的交流，并使用 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的一对人工智能模型对黄在出口限制问题上的立场以及他如何看待中国的每一条进行评分。

根据我们的评论，在中国的 DeepSeek 登上全球舞台以及华盛顿在 2025 年初对 Nvidia 对华销售施加新限制之前，黄仁勋在播客上以基本中立的语气谈到了出口限制，并将其视为合规问题。

在 2025 年的限制之后，黄仁勋在采访中提到中国的次数大约增加了六倍，这位芯片首席执行官认为，这些限制对美国的伤害比对中国的伤害更大。 “如果我们完全离开一个市场，毫无疑问其他人会介入，”他在 2025 年 5 月告诉迈克尔·米尔肯。

自 2025 年限制措施以来，他在 14 次采访中谈到了中国的人工智能研究人员、开源模型和制造业，这通常是美国无法承担与中国断绝关系的原因，或者拒绝将其视为敌人的想法。

自 2025 年 7 月以来，他在 8 次采访中 34 次引用了“美国技术堆栈”，认为世界开发者应该以美国技术为基础。他在八次采访中表示，世界上 50% 的人工智能研究人员是中国人或在中国，这表明该国的科技人才不容忽视。

news.title: Adobe’s AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters
news.title_en: Adobe’s AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Some of the most impressive tech that Adobe showcases at its annual Max conference each year is the experimental features it’s developing, and the latest of those tools are being announced today: they can transform images into explorable 3D scenes, design AI characters by talking to them, and turn photo editing into a copy/paste process.

The first (and weirdest, in my opinion) is Project Screen Test, which is designed to make AI-generated characters easier to develop and use for video content. Instead of just describing how the character should sound and behave in text prompts, the tool lets you talk to the character and direct them in an audition-like environment. You start by describing some base personality traits, such as “anxious, shy, awkward,” and giving the character a voice, either by selecting a preset, describing how it sounds in a prompt, or uploading sample audio for it to reference.

You can then expand its persona in further detail by conversing with the character as if you’re talking on FaceTime, outlining its backstory, temperament, goals, flaws, fears, movement quirks and more. Once you’re happy, the tool lets you generate animated screen tests with the character by describing an environment or scenario you want to put them in.

[Image: This Personality tab lets you manually adjust any of the traits that were generated for the character by talking to it. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/Screenshot-2026-11-11-085454.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

This is currently a standalone creative exercise, and it’s not clear how (or if) it could feature in any of Adobe’s existing AI video tools. The results provided a more identifiable and consistent personality compared to many soulless animated AI characters I’ve seen, but that’s the entire reason this exists — AI video generation provides far less creative control compared to traditional animation, where every aspect of a character is included with absolute intention.

There’s also Project Sight Span, which reframes photographs and images by turning them into a 3D environment that you can navigate through and reposition. The 3D space generates objects and backgrounds that are outside of the original frame, but feel like a natural part of the image, even if you’re turning to see what’s behind you. While the visuals in the 3D environment are pixelated and ill–defined, the resolution quality is restored when you select your chosen angle.

[Image: This still doesn’t really do Project Sight Span justice, but a video demonstration should take place at the Adobe Max sneaks keynote. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/Screenshot-2026-11-11-085101.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

Sight Span works with any flat image, including photos, paintings, and illustrations, and can preserve and replicate artistic styles. Even repositioned tattoos and facial features in photographs remain surprisingly recognizable and true to the original reference. It’s a bit like a version of Apple’s Spatial Reframing feature on steroids: you can reposition more aggressively and change the shooting point entirely if you want, but it also feels far less deserving of being called a photo afterward.

news.article_content_zh:
Adobe 每年在年度 Max 会议上展示的一些最令人印象深刻的技术是其正在开发的实验性功能，而这些工具中的最新功能今天即将发布：它们可以将图像转换为可探索的 3D 场景，通过与 AI 角色对话来设计它们，以及将照片编辑变成复制/粘贴过程。

第一个（在我看来也是最奇怪的）是 Project Screen Test，它旨在使人工智能生成的角色更容易开发和用于视频内容。该工具不仅可以在文本提示中描述角色的声音和行为，还可以让您与角色交谈并在类似试镜的环境中指导他们。首先描述一些基本的性格特征，例如“焦虑、害羞、尴尬”，然后通过选择预设、描述提示中的声音或上传示例音频以供参考，为角色提供声音。

然后，您可以通过与该角色交谈（就像在 FaceTime 上交谈一样）来进一步详细扩展其角色，概述其背景故事、气质、目标、缺陷、恐惧、动作怪癖等。一旦您感到满意，该工具就可以让您通过描述您想要将其放入的环境或场景来生成角色的动画屏幕测试。

目前，这是一项独立的创意活动，尚不清楚它如何（或是否）能够在 Adob​​e 现有的任何 AI 视频工具中发挥作用。与我见过的许多没有灵魂的动画人工智能角色相比，结果提供了更可识别和一致的个性，但这就是它存在的全部原因——与传统动画相比，人工智能视频生成提供的创意控制要少得多，传统动画中角色的每个方面都包含绝对意图。

还有 Project Sight Span，它可以将照片和图像转变为可以导航和重新定位的 3D 环境，从而重新构建照片和图像。 3D 空间生成原始框架之外的对象和背景，但感觉就像图像的自然部分，即使您转身看后面的东西也是如此。虽然 3D 环境中的视觉效果是像素化且不明确的，但当您选择所选角度时，分辨率质量会恢复。

Sight Span 适用于任何平面图像，包括照片、绘画和插图，并且可以保留和复制艺术风格。即使照片中重新定位的纹身和面部特征仍然令人惊讶地可识别，并且与原始参考相符。这有点像苹果空间重构功能的增强版本：如果你愿意，你可以更积极地重新定位并完全改变拍摄点，但它也让人感觉根本不值得被称为照片。

Project Sound Bender 是一项 AI 音频混合功能，可让您自定义音效，就像在色轮周围单击光标一样。它的工作原理是上传视频剪辑，然后在文本提示中描述您想要的音频，例如“冒泡的科幻大锅噪音”。然后，Sound Bender 会生成声音效果并自动将其同步到视频，并提供方形声音画布，让您可以实时调整噪音。画布的每个角落都会自动分配一个相关的人工智能生成的声音，比如密集的汩汩声和爆破的气泡声、隆隆的沸腾岩石声、尖锐的布洛普声和噼啪作响的电火声。您可以在画布上拖动光标来选择最突出的噪音，或使用不同的声音效果自定义每个角落。

Adobe 还展示了 Project Rinse Repeat，它允许您复制编辑内容，然后自动将它们应用到同一张照片中的其他对象或人物。例如，如果您煞费苦心地用喷枪去除一个人身上的痤疮或瑕疵，“冲洗重复”功能会将您的具体更改调整到一组需要类似修饰的其他人身上。它还可用于在营销图形中为产品添加阴影，即使对象具有不同的形状和大小。 Rinse Repeat 是围绕 Photoshop 构建的，您应用于其他主题的编辑仍然完全可编辑，因为该工具使用本机 Photoshop 工具重新创建它们。

这些“先睹为快”是功能的技术预览，最终可能会开发成 Adob​​e Creative Cloud 应用程序或 Firefly 平台的工具，因此不能保证它们会逐渐成为可用功能。然而，几乎所有这些项目都是围绕 Adob​​e 的生成式 AI 开发而构建的，并且鉴于 AI 工具现在在该公司的增长战略中发挥着核心作用，因此至少其中一些实验可能会正式启动。尽管这些人工智能实验既古怪又有趣，但它们也是一个预兆。如果它们足够有用，这意味着人工智能最终可能会取代创意专业人士目前使用的工具和库存库，无论他们对这项技术的感受有多复杂。

news.title: US data brokers are selling half a billion dollars in RL training environments to Chinese AI labs
news.title_en: US data brokers are selling half a billion dollars in RL training environments to Chinese AI labs
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
American data brokers sell so-called RL environments to Chinese AI labs, helping them save compute during model development. A ChinaTalk investigation identifies at least nine companies involved.

American data firms like Mercor, Surge AI, AfterQuery, and Turing are selling roughly half a billion dollars' worth of training data to Chinese AI labs, according to an investigation by ChinaTalk. Some of that data takes the form of reinforcement learning environments, which are simulated worlds where AI models are trained on specific tasks like coding, financial analysis, or office work.

Chinese labs deliberately buy the same products previously sold to Anthropic or OpenAI, the report says. That way, they already know the data works and can skip costly in-house development and wasted training runs. Because Chinese chips suffer from acute memory bottlenecks, those savings are particularly valuable for labs there.

There is also the issue of distillation. Chinese labs use powerful US models like GPT or Claude as "teachers," using their outputs as training examples. Combined with purchased RL environments, this creates a two-pronged advantage that lets Chinese labs close the gap with less compute of their own.

The authors identified at least nine US data firms selling to Chinese customers. AfterQuery reportedly draws a significant share of its annual recurring revenue from Chinese customers. ChinaTalk points to Forbes reports of about $100 million in ARR but could not independently verify the sales.

Surge AI openly advertises on its website that its products are "built by the same experts behind our frontier-lab work." The deals also run through offshore structures. ByteDance maintains procurement offices in Singapore and San Jose.

These business relationships came to light through a combination of anonymous sources and sloppy operational security among subcontractors, according to ChinaTalk. The US data firms outsource much of the actual RL environment creation and data curation to low-paid workers in developing countries, especially India. Those subcontractors then sometimes post client names on LinkedIn or in résumés, even though they are supposed to use only code names. Export controls barely apply because RL environments remain largely unregulated.

Domains with dual-use potential pose particular risks: Coding environments improve software development but can also sharpen offensive cyber capabilities. Biology environments could improve gene synthesis capabilities and potentially enhance bioweapons-relevant applications. The ChinaTalk authors argue that the Bureau of Industry and Security should subject these dual-use environments to existing export controls.

At the same time, the authors stress that these relationships are not apocalyptic. By piggybacking on US work, Chinese labs still trail their US peers by at least a few months as a structural matter. Sensitive environments in areas like biology, chemistry, cybersecurity, chip design, and investment banking are increasingly being built in-house at American frontier companies, the authors say.

美国数据经纪人向中国人工智能实验室出售所谓的强化学习环境，帮助他们在模型开发过程中节省计算量。 ChinaTalk 的一项调查发现至少有 9 家公司参与其中。

根据 ChinaTalk 的一项调查，Mercor、Surge AI、AfterQuery 和 Turing 等美国数据公司正在向中国人工智能实验室出售价值约 5 亿美元的训练数据。其中一些数据采用强化学习环境的形式，这些环境是模拟世界，人工智能模型在其中接受编码、财务分析或办公室工作等特定任务的训练。

报告称，中国实验室故意购买之前出售给 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 的相同产品。这样，他们就已经知道数据的工作原理，并且可以跳过昂贵的内部开发和浪费的培训运行。由于中国芯片存在严重的内存瓶颈，因此这些节省对于那里的实验室来说特别有价值。

还有蒸馏的问题。中国实验室使用 GPT 或 Claude 等强大的美国模型作为“老师”，使用它们的输出作为训练示例。与购买的强化学习环境相结合，这创造了一个双管齐下的优势，让中国实验室可以用更少的计算来缩小差距。

作者确定了至少九家向中国客户销售产品的美国数据公司。据报道，AfterQuery 的年度经常性收入中有很大一部分来自中国客户。 ChinaTalk 指出《福布斯》报道称 ARR 约为 1 亿美元，但无法独立核实销售额。

Surge AI 在其网站上公开宣传其产品“由我们前沿实验室工作背后的同一位专家打造”。这些交易还通过离岸结构进行。字节跳动在新加坡和圣何塞设有采购办事处。

据 ChinaTalk 报道，这些业务关系是通过匿名消息来源和分包商之间草率的运营安全的结合而曝光的。美国数据公司将大部分实际的强化学习环境创建和数据管理外包给发展中国家（尤其是印度）的低薪工人。这些分包商有时会在 LinkedIn 或简历中发布客户姓名，尽管他们应该只使用代号。出口管制几乎不适用，因为强化学习环境在很大程度上仍然不受监管。

具有双重用途潜力的领域会带来特殊的风险：编码环境可以改善软件开发，但也可以增强进攻性网络能力。生物环境可以提高基因合成能力，并有可能增强生物武器相关的应用。 ChinaTalk 的作者认为，工业和安全局应该将这些双重用途环境置于现有的出口管制之下。

同时，作者强调这些关系并不是世界末日。通过借助美国的研究成果，中国实验室在结构性问题上仍然落后美国同行至少几个月。作者表示，生物、化学、网络安全、芯片设计和投资银行等领域的敏感环境越来越多地在美国前沿公司内部建立。

【起因与机理】中国实验室为绕过研发试错成本并缓解高端芯片短缺带来的内存瓶颈
【关键数据与实测】美方经纪商向中方出售价值5亿的RL训练资源。
【观点态度】此举变相缩短了中美模型的技术差距。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To bypass expensive R&D trial-and-error and mitigate local compute memory bottlenecks

news.title: DeepL wants real-time translation to finally capture sarcasm and mood shifts
news.title_en: DeepL wants real-time translation to finally capture sarcasm and mood shifts
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
DeepL Voice's real-time translations are about to sound a lot more natural. The company's new Aure model carries over tone, emotion, emphasis, and speaking pace from the original speaker's voice into the target language. Until now, DeepL Voice generated translated speech from a static voice sample captured at the start of a conversation. That meant it couldn't pick up on mood shifts or sarcasm. Aure works differently, continuously analyzing both the translated text and the original audio as the conversation unfolds.

During training, DeepL separates voice identity, speech melody, and content so each component can be transferred into the new language independently. Reinforcement learning keeps accents out of the output. Aure runs automatically in DeepL Voice for Online Meetings, In-Person Conversations, and the DeepL API. At launch, the model supports English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, and Korean.

DeepL first rolled out voice preservation in September. In May, the company cut about 250 jobs to restructure around smaller, AI-powered teams as part of what it called becoming an "AI-native" company. DeepL also acquired the team behind audio streaming specialist Mixhalo to bolster its real-time speech translation. Block is chasing a similar goal of capturing meaning beyond words. The company recently unveiled Dessa, a speech model designed to detect emotions and sarcasm directly from audio.

news.article_content_zh:
DeepL Voice 的实时翻译听起来会更加自然。该公司的新 Aure 模型将语气、情感、重点和语速从原始说话者的声音转移到目标语言中。到目前为止，DeepL Voice 从对话开始时捕获的静态语音样本生成翻译后的语音。这意味着它无法捕捉到情绪变化或讽刺。 Aure 的工作方式有所不同，它会随着对话的展开不断分析翻译文本和原始音频。

在训练过程中，DeepL 将语音身份、语音旋律和内容分开，因此每个组件都可以独立地转换为新语言。强化学习将口音排除在输出之外。 Aure 在 DeepL Voice 中自动运行，用于在线会议、面对面对话和 DeepL API。发布时，该模型支持英语、德语、西班牙语、法语、意大利语、日语、葡萄牙语和韩语。

DeepL 在 9 月份首次推出了语音保存功能。 5 月份，该公司裁员约 250 人，以围绕更小的人工智能团队进行重组，作为其所谓的“人工智能本土”公司的一部分。 DeepL 还收购了音频流专家 Mixhalo 背后的团队，以增强其实时语音翻译能力。布洛克也在追求类似的目标，即捕捉文字之外的意义。该公司最近推出了 Dessa，这是一种旨在直接从音频中检测情绪和讽刺的语音模型。

【起因与机理】旨在提升翻译的自然度，解决原有静态语音无法表达讽刺与情绪起伏的问题
【关键技术规格】DeepL引入Aure模型升级语音实时翻译。
【观点态度】应用于在线会议与API等多场景。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To eliminate the robotic nature of previous versions and enable the translation of nuanced moods and sarcasm
[Key Specification] DeepL introduces Aure model for real-time voice translation.
[Perspective & Impact] Deployed across online meetings and API platforms.

news.title: The Download: preserving minds and weighing open AI risks
news.title_en: The Download: preserving minds and weighing open AI risks
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
As we age, we forget most of what we’ve experienced, yet there’s still undeniable continuity: At 30, or 50, or 70, you will still be you.

To preserve that elusive continuity of self, some far-thinking technologists are exploring ways to keep the brain going, even beyond death. Their ideas range from freezing brains in liquid nitrogen to augmenting living ones and uploading our memories to the cloud.

Here are six possible paths for keeping your mind going, and how feasible they might be.

Anthropic recently released a report arguing that a powerful new model released by the Chinese company Z.ai, poses a major cyberattack risk. Its core concern was that it is freely available for anyone to download and modify.

The warning was the latest flashpoint in the debate over open frontier AI models. Critics warn that bad actors can misuse them, while supporters argue they prevent a handful of companies from controlling the technology. The debate, however, is more complicated than it seems.

This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 COP31’s flagship pledge to electrify 35% of energy use is sinkingOnly around a dozen nations are reportedly ready to sign it. (Politico)+ It requires quadrupling the pace of electrification. (New Scientist $)+ John Kerry says the US must follow China on clean energy. (Guardian)+ But the US skipped the talks entirely for a second year. (NYT $)+ What’s the future of electricity? (MIT Technology Review)

2 The Nvidia spy scandal reportedly involves $7.5 billion of chipsAlice Huang allegedly obtained 240,000 restricted chips. (Information $)+ Trump was told of Huang’s spy link on Air Force One. (NYT $)+ Experts warn the scandal could erode America’s AI lead. (Verge)+ Nvidia’s slide has let Microsoft overtake it in value. (Reuters $)

3 Studies found AI agents go rogue because they’re “incorrigible”Their training rewards them for finishing tasks at any cost. (NYT $)+ This is why AI agents lie and cheat to reach their goals. (MIT Technology Review)

4 Anthropic has scaled back its IPO valuation to $1.4 trillionIt aimed for $2 trillion before the recent AI jitters. (Guardian)

5 Drone strikes have wiped out 3% of Yandex’s cloud customer dataUkraine hit three of its data centers in October. (Reuters $)+ Ukraine’s drones are fighting data centers for fiber. (Ars Technica)

6 Moderna says its new vaccine could prevent cancer in high-risk peopleThe company’s CEO calls it the “holy grail” of cancer prevention. (FT $)+ Hong Kong is testing a next-gen ultrasound cancer treatment. (SCMP)

7 Scientists have slowly reversed human cells’ ages by decadesOne age marker was set back as far as 60 years. (Wired $)+ “Reprogramming” is the buzziest de-aging idea. (MIT Technology Review)

8 Robot vessels are hunting for mines in the Strait of HormuzAI helps them spot mines camouflaged on the seabed. (BBC)

9 Life may have started inside a tiny bubbleThat’s the idea behind the “lipid first” origin theory. (Quanta)

10 As Voyager 1 reaches a light day from Earth, here's what it's taught usIts discoveries rewrote textbooks in real time. (New Scientist $)

—Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, accuses President Do...

news.article_content_zh:
随着年龄的增长，我们会忘记大部分经历过的事情，但不可否认的是，连续性仍然存在：30岁、50岁或70岁时，你仍然是你。

为了保持这种难以捉摸的自我连续性，一些有远见的技术专家正在探索如何让大脑保持运转，甚至在死亡之后也能继续运转。他们的想法涵盖从在液氮中冷冻大脑到增强活体大脑以及将我们的记忆上传到云端等。

这里有六种可能的方法可以帮助你保持思维活跃，以及它们的可行性。

Anthropic 最近发布了一份报告，认为中国公司 Z.ai 发布的强大新模型构成了重大网络攻击风险。它的核心关注点是任何人都可以免费下载和修改。

这一警告是开放前沿人工智能模型争论中的最新热点。批评者警告说，不良行为者可能会滥用它们，而支持者则认为它们会阻止少数公司控制该技术。然而，这场争论比看起来更复杂。

这是我们最新的故事，将成为《麻省理工学院技术评论》解说播客，每周都会在 Spotify 和 Apple 播客上发布。只需在任一平台上导航至《麻省理工学院技术评论叙述》，然后关注我们即可获取发布的所有新内容。

我梳理了互联网，为您找到当今最有趣/最重要/最可怕/最迷人的技术故事。

1 COP31 关于实现 35% 能源使用电气化的旗舰承诺正在落空 据报道，只有大约十几个国家准备签署该承诺。 (Politico)+ 它需要将电气化速度提高四倍。 (New Scientist $)+ 约翰·克里表示，美国必须在清洁能源方面追随中国。 （卫报）+ 但美国连续第二年完全跳过了谈判。 (NYT $)+ 电力的未来是什么？ （麻省理工科技评论）

2 据报道，Nvidia 间谍丑闻涉及价值 75 亿美元的芯片 Alice Huang 据称获得了 24 万块受限芯片。 (信息$)+ 特朗普被告知黄在空军一号上有间谍联系。 (NYT $)+ 专家警告称，这一丑闻可能会削弱美国在人工智能领域的领先地位。 (Verge)+ 英伟达的下滑让微软在价值上超越了它。 （路透社$）

3 研究发现，人工智能代理之所以会变得无赖，是因为他们“无可救药”。他们的训练会奖励他们不惜一切代价完成任务。 (NYT $)+ 这就是人工智能代理为了达到目标而撒谎和欺骗的原因。 （麻省理工科技评论）

4 Anthropic 已将其 IPO 估值缩减至 1.4 万亿美元，在最近的人工智能动荡之前，其目标是 2 万亿美元。 （监护人）

5 无人机袭击摧毁了 Yandex 3% 的云客户数据 乌克兰 10 月份袭击了其三个数据中心。 (Reuters $)+ 乌克兰的无人机正在与数据中心争夺光纤。 （Ars Technica）

6 Moderna 称其新疫苗可以预防高危人群的癌症 该公司首席执行官称其为预防癌症的“圣杯”。 (FT $)+ 香港正在测试下一代超声波癌症治疗方法。 （南华早报）

7 科学家已将人类细胞的年龄缓慢逆转了数十年，其中一个年龄标记已被推迟了 60 岁。 (Wired $)+ “重新编程”是最流行的抗衰老想法。 （麻省理工科技评论）

news.title: Grok-built apps exposed patient data, plaintext passwords, and SpaceXSI's own sales pipeline
news.title_en: Grok-built apps exposed patient data, plaintext passwords, and SpaceXSI's own sales pipeline
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Apps built with the AI assistant Grok are almost always open to anyone with the link, according to a security firm. The exposed data includes patient records and confidential documents from Grok maker SpaceXSI itself.

Security firm Claroc found more than 35,000 Grok-built apps that could be accessed without login, according to a recent report. In SpaceXSI's "Build" mode (the company was formerly xAI), users describe an app in a chat and Grok writes the code. An app only goes public when its creator clicks "Publish," which gives it its own address on grok.me.

Out of 37,571 apps Claroc checked that were still online, 35,578 were open to anyone. That's 94.7 percent, according to the report. Claroc points to the publish dialog as the cause. On the paid account the firm used for testing, "Anyone with the link" was already preselected. The addresses were also easy to find. Each app gets its own subdomain, so its name shows up in commercial passive DNS databases after the first visit. Those databases can be searched by pattern.

24 of the accessible apps came from SpaceXSI and X employees. Among them was a confidential onboarding plan for a new enterprise sales team member that included internal system addresses and 19 chat channels. Claroc also found a publicly accessible sales territory map with 594 strategic accounts and pipeline data, plus eight X ad proposals. One of those proposals targeted a U.S. federal agency and was marked as confidential. Campaign reports and dashboards with ad spending were also exposed.

Most of the open apps were games, landing pages, or calculators, Claroc says. But about one in ten contained sensitive material, internal business data, or personal information. The firm classifies roughly two percent as especially bad. The researchers estimate that 650 to 800 apps contained private data.

Confirmed cases included an ICU briefing with a patient's lab values, a list of more than 3,500 employees at a hospital group, and a fire department shift schedule. The source code of a timesheet app contained 18 accounts with plaintext passwords. Beyond SpaceXSI and X, Claroc identified 30 affected organizations, six of them Fortune 500 companies. The firm is withholding the names.

Two of Claroc's own test apps turned up another problem. A contact list app ended up with a database that had no login, so anonymous visitors could add entries. For a sales team customer list, Grok added Google and X sign-in on its own. In that test app, though, Grok's code added every authenticated user to the team first and only checked membership afterward. An outside Google account could then read, edit, and delete records. Claroc says it ran write and delete tests only on its own apps.

Grok does offer the right settings. When set to "Only you," the test app blocked outside access. It just isn't the default. In a test with ChatGPT, a newly built app defaulted to "Only me" when shared. That app's address can also show up in DNS data, but it leads to an app only the owner can open.

SpaceXSI responded to the disclosure only by saying that apps are private until their creator shares them, that publishing takes multiple steps including a legal notice, and that employee accounts default to "Only you." Claroc counters that extra clicks don't help if "Anyone with the link" is still preselected at the final step. The 24 open employee apps also show how little the stricter default for staff accounts actually helps, the firm says.

news.title_zh: Grok开发的AI应用致海量数据泄露
news.summary_zh: 安全机构发现95%通过Grok生成的应用未设访问权限，导致患者医疗数据及企业内部销售文档被公开
news.article_content_zh:
据一家安全公司称，用人工智能助手Grok开发的应用程序几乎总是对任何有链接的人开放。暴露的数据包括患者记录和Grok制造商SpaceXSI本身的机密文件。

根据最近的一份报告，安全公司 Claroc 发现了超过 35,000 个 Grok 构建的应用程序无需登录即可访问。在 SpaceXSI 的“构建”模式（该公司以前称为 xAI）中，用户在聊天中描述应用程序，然后 Grok 编写代码。应用程序只有在其创建者单击“发布”时才会公开，这会在 grok.me 上为其提供自己的地址。

在 Claroc 检查的 37,571 个仍然在线的应用程序中，有 35,578 个对任何人开放。报告称，这一比例为 94.7%。 Claroc 指出发布对话框是原因。在该公司用于测试的付费帐户上，已经预先选择了“知道链接的任何人”。地址也很容易找到。每个应用程序都有自己的子域，因此其名称在第一次访问后会显示在商业被动 DNS 数据库中。可以按模式搜索这些数据库。

其中 24 个可访问的应用程序来自 SpaceXSI 和 X 员工。其中包括针对新企业销售团队成员的保密入职计划，其中包括内部系统地址和 19 个聊天渠道。 Claroc 还发现了一个可公开访问的销售区域地图，其中包含 594 个战略客户和渠道数据，以及 8 个 X 广告提案。其中一项提案针对美国联邦机构，并被标记为机密。广告支出的活动报告和仪表板也被曝光。

克拉洛克说，大多数打开的应用程序都是游戏、登陆页面或计算器。但大约十分之一包含敏感材料、内部业务数据或个人信息。该公司将大约百分之二的情况列为特别糟糕。研究人员估计 650 至 800 个应用程序包含私人数据。

确诊病例包括 ICU 简报，其中包含患者的实验室数据、医院集团 3,500 多名员工的名单以及消防部门的轮班时间表。时间表应用程序的源代码包含 18 个带有明文密码的帐户。除了 SpaceXSI 和 X 之外，Claroc 还确定了 30 个受影响的组织，其中 6 个是财富 500 强公司。该公司拒绝透露姓名。

Claroc 自己的两个测试应用程序又出现了另一个问题。联系人列表应用程序最终会获得一个无需登录的数据库，因此匿名访问者可以添加条目。对于销售团队客户列表，Grok 自行添加了 Google 和 X 登录。不过，在该测试应用程序中，Grok 的代码首先将每个经过身份验证的用户添加到团队中，然后才检查成员资格。然后，外部 Google 帐户可以读取、编辑和删除记录。 Claroc 表示，它只在自己的应用程序上运行写入和删除测试。

Grok 确实提供了正确的设置。当设置为“仅限您”时，测试应用程序会阻止外部访问。它只是不是默认值。在使用 ChatGPT 进行的测试中，新建的应用程序在共享时默认为“仅我”。该应用程序的地址也可以显示在 DNS 数据中，但它会导致只有所有者才能打开的应用程序。

SpaceXSI 对这一披露的回应只是表示，应用程序在其创建者分享之前都是私有的，发布需要采取多个步骤，包括法律声明，并且员工帐户默认为“只有你”。 Claroc 反驳说，如果在最后一步仍然预先选择“知道链接的任何人”，那么额外的点击并没有什么帮助。该公司表示，24 个开放的员工应用程序还表明，对员工账户实行更严格的默认设置实际上没有什么帮助。

克拉洛克建议 SpaceXSI 将“只有你”设置为默认值，并在发布前显示谁可以访问。当应用程序有数据库但没有登录时，Grok 还应该发出警告。应用程序应该在共享主机上难以猜测的路径上运行，而不是单独的子域，这样它们的名称就不会出现在 DNS 数据中。

此后，SpaceXSI 已将 24 个员工应用程序下线，但尚未删除其他 Grok 用户和组织的开放应用程序。克拉洛克提出愿意秘密分享完整的地址列表。由于 SpaceXSI 没有承诺联系受影响的所有者，Claroc 现在直接通知他们。该公司在这里有自己的利益。它销售人工智能构建的应用程序的安全解决方案。

这至少是 SpaceXSI 涉及 Grok 的第三起隐私事件。 2025 年 8 月，《福布斯》在 Google 搜索中发现了超过 370,000 个共享的 Grok 对话。 2026 年 7 月，终端工具 Grok Build 在未经询问的情况下将用户文件上传到公司服务器，包括 SSH 密钥和密码数据库。由于 Grok 产生的性化深度假货，爱尔兰数据保护机构也在调查 X 是否在设计上忽视了数据保护。

其他提供商的共享功能也有类似的问题。使用相同的被动 DNS 方法，Claroc 在 10 月份追踪到了来自 Meta 代理 Muse 的约 6,800 个共享对话。在 Anthropic，共享的 Claude 聊天记录和工件于 7 月份出现在搜索引擎中，包括用户构建的应用程序。

news.title: Game developer House House confirms using AI during Big Walk's final development, sparking an intense debate among Independent Games Festival judges and jurors (Luke Plunkett/Aftermath)
news.title_en: Game developer House House confirms using AI during Big Walk's final development, sparking an intense debate among Independent Games Festival judges and jurors (Luke Plunkett/Aftermath)
news.author: Aftermath
news.article_content:
Published: November 10, 2026, 1:32 am Last updated: November 10, 2026, 6:49 am | Share When a number of IGF jurors took a hard stance on AI-developed video games yesterday we wrote a fairly standard blog about the news, but not long after the story was first published some additional, and deeply divisive, discussions emerged concerning one of the best video games of the year.

While the IGF jurors did not name any games in particular when outlining their opposition, it only took a few hours for news to emerge across social media that one of (if not the) biggest contributors to the "fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools" was the revelation that Big Walk had used AI "in the final stretch" of the game's development.

Developers House House told Aftermath via email that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that they "estimate that well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage". They also stress that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game".

House House also say they understand opposition to the news, adding "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as 'inevitable'. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards."

Despite this seemingly minor use of AI, the fact remains the game used AI in development, which for some in the IGF jury pool (and beyond) was clearly a huge disappointment, especially given the game's other progressive stances. For others, however, it's merely a sign of the times, or an instance where people's distrust and exhaustion with the tech was causing them to alienate a game that otherwise will be among many shortlists for GOTY.

As for why House House is only confirming AI use in the game now, rather than at release, they say "We have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage. We are posting this disclosure as it has become a matter of public interest."

For future games, the studio says "Big Walk was developed without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards."

Luke Plunkett Luke Plunkett is a co-founder of the website Aftermath.

news.summary_zh: 独立游戏开发商House House承认在《Big Walk》最后开发阶段使用了AI修复Bug，引发独立游戏节评委团的激烈争议
news.article_content_zh:
发布时间：2026 年 11 月 10 日凌晨 1:32 最后更新时间：2026 年 11 月 10 日上午 6:49 |昨天，当一些 IGF 评审员对人工智能开发的视频游戏采取强硬立场时，我们写了一篇关于该新闻的相当标准的博客，但在该报道首次发表后不久，出现了一些关于年度最佳视频游戏之一的额外且严重分歧的讨论。

虽然 IGF 陪审员在概述他们的反对意见时没有特别点名任何游戏，但几个小时后，社交媒体上就出现了消息，称“法官和陪审团之间相当激烈的讨论和分歧”的最大贡献者之一（如果不是的话）是 Big Walk 在游戏开发的“最后阶段”使用了人工智能。

开发人员 House House 通过电子邮件告诉 Aftermath，“House House 很少使用法学硕士来帮助解决困难的技术挑战和错误”，并且他们“估计 Big Walk 的代码中远低于 0.1% 的代码与这种使用有关”。他们还强调，“在制作游戏时，生成式人工智能并未在任何其他环境中使用”。

House House 还表示，他们理解对这一消息的反对意见，并补充道，“我们担心这样的自愿披露可能会导致这项技术的正常化，或者将其视为‘不可避免’。我们支持那些试图限制生成式人工智能对视频游戏和我们的世界造成的危害的人们的工作，并对 Big Walk 的法学硕士使用可能不符合他们的标准表示歉意。”

尽管人工智能的使用看似很少，但事实仍然是游戏在开发中使用了人工智能，这对于 IGF 评审团（及其他成员）中的一些人来说显然是一个巨大的失望，特别是考虑到游戏的其他进步立场。然而，对于其他人来说，这只是时代的标志，或者是人们对技术的不信任和疲惫导致他们疏远这款游戏的一个例子，否则这款游戏将跻身《GOTY》众多候选名单之列。

至于为什么 House House 现在才确认游戏中人工智能的使用，而不是在发布时确认，他们表示“我们没有在 Steam 上进行任何披露，因为该平台不要求披露代码或聊天机器人的使用情况。我们发布此披露是因为它已成为公共利益问题。”

对于未来的游戏，该工作室表示“Big Walk 的开发没有制定内部人工智能使用政策，我们认为缺乏政策是一种失败。我们将努力制定更全面的政策。”

news.title: Enterprise sales push OpenAI's quarterly revenue to $10 billion, though it still trails Anthropic
news.title_en: Enterprise sales push OpenAI's quarterly revenue to $10 billion, though it still trails Anthropic
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
OpenAI posts a massive Q3 revenue jump, driven by new AI models and enterprise customers. But operating losses keep growing, while rival Anthropic operates far more efficiently ahead of its IPO.

According to reports from the Wall Street Journal and The Information, OpenAI grew its revenue by about 50 percent quarter over quarter in Q3 to $10 billion. In Q2, revenue had grown by just 17 to 18 percent. A year earlier, the company brought in $3.9 billion.

Despite tripling revenue within a year, adjusted operating losses rose slightly in Q3 from $10.1 billion to $10.9 billion. That figure doesn't include stock-based compensation, which climbed to $2.6 billion. The adjusted operating margin did improve, going from negative 150 percent in Q2 to negative 109 percent. A year earlier it was negative 97 percent.

That puts OpenAI behind industry leader Anthropic, which plans its IPO next week. The Claude developer already overtook OpenAI on revenue in Q2 and even posted a small operating profit at the time. In Q3, Anthropic grew revenue 47 percent to $17 billion, while its operating loss including stock compensation came to just $567 million.

The efficiency gap comes down to business models. Anthropic focuses heavily on enterprise customers and successful tools like Claude Code and the Claude Cowork agent. OpenAI, by contrast, funds broad research into robotics and runs an expensive consumer business.

To catch up in the enterprise market, OpenAI reshuffled its priorities earlier this year. The company discontinued projects like a video app, put more resources into its coding tool Codex, and hired Dali Rajic as its new head of sales. At the same time, OpenAI cut prices on new models.

Third-party data showed companies seeking cheaper alternatives to Claude, which boosted API sales. OpenAI president Greg Brockman called it an incredible revenue turning point and pointed to major customers like JPMorgan Chase. The enterprise business doubled in Q3 and now accounts for the bulk of revenue, Brockman said.

Both competitors are feeling the recent tech sell-off in the financial markets. OpenAI is targeting an IPO next year and is currently raising fresh capital at a $1.25 trillion valuation, but has so far raised less than half of the planned $30 billion. Anthropic also had to cut its IPO valuation target significantly.

news.article_content_zh:
在新的人工智能模型和企业客户的推动下，OpenAI 第三季度收入大幅增长。但运营亏损不断增加，而竞争对手 Anthropic 在 IPO 之前运营效率要高得多。

据《华尔街日报》和《The Information》报道，OpenAI 第三季度营收环比增长约 50%，达到 100 亿美元。第二季度，收入仅增长了 17% 至 18%。一年前，该公司实现收入 39 亿美元。

尽管收入在一年内增长了两倍，但第三季度调整后的运营亏损从 101 亿美元小幅上升至 109 亿美元。这个数字不包括基于股票的薪酬，该薪酬已攀升至 26 亿美元。调整后的营业利润率确实有所改善，从第二季度的负 150% 降至负 109%。一年前，这一数字为负 97%。

这使得 OpenAI 落后于行业领导者 Anthropic，该公司计划下周进行 IPO。 Claude 开发商在第二季度的收入上已经超过了 OpenAI，甚至当时还公布了小幅营业利润。第三季度，Anthropic 的收入增长了 47%，达到 170 亿美元，而包括股票补偿在内的运营亏损仅为 5.67 亿美元。

效率差距归结于商业模式。 Anthropic 重点关注企业客户和 Claude Code 和 Claude Cowork 代理等成功工具。相比之下，OpenAI 资助了对机器人技术的广泛研究，并经营着昂贵的消费业务。

为了赶上企业市场，OpenAI 在今年早些时候重新调整了其优先事项。该公司终止了视频应用程序等项目，将更多资源投入其编码工具 Codex，并聘请 Dali Rajic 担任新的销售主管。与此同时，OpenAI 对新机型进行了降价。

第三方数据显示，公司正在寻求更便宜的 Claude 替代品，这促进了 API 销售。 OpenAI 总裁格雷格·布罗克曼 (Greg Brockman) 称这是一个令人难以置信的收入转折点，并指出了摩根大通等主要客户。布罗克曼表示，企业业务在第三季度翻了一番，目前占收入的大部分。

两家竞争对手都感受到了金融市场最近科技股的抛售。 OpenAI 的目标是明年进行 IPO，目前正在以 1.25 万亿美元的估值筹集新资金，但迄今为止筹集的资金还不到计划 300 亿美元的一半。 Anthropic 还不得不大幅下调 IPO 估值目标。

news.title: UK regulator threatens universities with sanctions unless they adopt AI-proof exam formats
news.title_en: UK regulator threatens universities with sanctions unless they adopt AI-proof exam formats
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
AI makes it "close to impossible" to fairly grade student coursework, England's higher-education regulator the Office for Students (OfS) says. The agency is urging universities to bring back traditional exams and in-person presentations, the Guardian reports.

A joint OfS and Advance HE survey of more than 300 respondents at 127 institutions found students use AI heavily for essays and dissertations — often undetected — and receive similar grades to those working without it. Some students wrote entire papers with ChatGPT and couldn't recall basic content afterward, the report says, while instructors describe large batches of uniform submissions sharing identical sources and style.

OfS strategy director Josh Fleming called this a "generational risk," saying it threatens the credibility of degrees, and demanded "far greater use of AI-free assessment." The OfS warns it could sanction institutions that don't develop reliable formats. Many universities are already moving toward oral exams, process-based assessments, or tasks where students critically revise AI-generated text. Britain's Department for Education expects universities "to take this issue seriously" and wants the OfS to ensure its regulatory framework is "explicit, strong and durable on the use of AI."

news.article_content_zh:
英国高等教育监管机构学生办公室 (OfS) 表示，人工智能使得对学生课程作业进行公平评分“几乎不可能”。据《卫报》报道，该机构正在敦促大学恢复传统考试和现场演示。

OfS 和 Advance HE 联合对 127 所机构的 300 多名受访者进行了调查发现，学生在论文和论文中大量使用人工智能（通常未被发现），并且获得与没有使用人工智能的学生相似的成绩。报告称，一些学生用 ChatGPT 写了整篇论文，但后来记不起基本内容，而教师则描述了大批量的统一提交，共享相同的来源和风格。

OfS 战略总监乔什·弗莱明 (Josh Fleming) 称这是“代际风险”，威胁到学位的可信度，并要求“更多地使用无人工智能的评估”。 OfS 警告称，它可能会制裁那些不开发可靠格式的机构。许多大学已经转向口试、基于流程的评估或学生批判性地修改人工智能生成文本的任务。英国教育部希望大学“认真对待这个问题”，并希望英国教育部确保其在人工智能使用方面的监管框架“明确、强大和持久”。

news.title: Sources: the UK's proposed under-16 social media ban is expanding to target recommender systems and user content, including YouTube Kids, Lego Play, and Spotify (Jessica Elgot/The Guardian)
news.title_en: Sources: the UK's proposed under-16 social media ban is expanding to target recommender systems and user content, including YouTube Kids, Lego Play, and Spotify (Jessica Elgot/The Guardian)
news.author: The Guardian
news.article_content:
The online safety minister, Ian Murray, said platforms must prevent harms being created by algorithms, recommender systems or conversations that can be had with strangers. Photograph: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen The online safety minister, Ian Murray, said platforms must prevent harms being created by algorithms, recommender systems or conversations that can be had with strangers. Photograph: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Shutterstock UK social media ban expansion for under-16s could cover YouTube KidsRegulations under consideration could affect up to 150 platforms, including LegoPlay, Spotify and eBay, sources say

A substantial expansion of the social media ban for under-16s could inadvertently lead to a ban on YouTube Kids and other sites that had been thought exempt, sources briefed on the government’s proposals have said.

One source close to the talks said the regulations now under consideration meant up to 150 platforms, including games platforms such as Lego Play, could be covered by the ban, which is set to come into force in March.

The regulations will be sent for cabinet signoff this week, and the culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, is expected to lay them in parliament in December.

Ministers are understood to be keen for a catch-all approach that limits ban workarounds. Critics of Australia’s social media prohibition say teenagers have switched to new platforms or found innovative ways of messaging using other seemingly innocuous sites.

Tech companies, industry groups and MPs have been briefed that the government’s working proposal focuses on recommender systems and user-generated content.

Spotify – which has some user-generated content and shows recommended music or podcasts – could technically be in scope if those proposals are enacted, though the music streaming site has sought reassurances that it would not face a ban because it is not primarily a social platform.

One industry source said: “We all share the goal of keeping teenagers safe online. Proposals have to be workable, and a situation where eBay, Lego, YouTube Kids and Spotify aren’t clear whether they comply is unsustainable. Detailed guidelines can’t come soon enough.”

Another said: “The whole internet has a recommender system. The regulation is just too broad. But they want to make it really broad and legally airtight so they can be prepared for any eventuality.”

Companies are expected to be briefed on the final proposal in the coming days by the Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) and No 10.

When the ban was announced by Keir Starmer in June, the government said it would ensure the ban did not include educational services, e-commerce platforms or music streaming, saying there would be “a narrowly defined list of exemptions to the definitions which will be kept under review”.

But tech companies are understood to be telling the government that removing the recommender algorithm would make it impossible for their sites to function.

The regulations do not require primary legislation in the House of Commons, and will be tabled as an addition to the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Act.

Ministers are also looking at a second tranche of regulations in the spring which could cover e-commerce platforms such as Vinted, eBay and Depop. MPs and campaigners have raised concerns with Nandy that teenagers and groomers can find innovative ways to communicate on platforms that allow unknown or anonymous user messaging, such as those...

news.article_content_zh:
网络安全部长伊恩·穆雷 (Ian Murray) 表示，平台必须防止算法、推荐系统或与陌生人的对话造成的伤害。照片：Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Shutterstock 全屏查看图像 在线安全部长 Ian Murray 表示，平台必须防止算法、推荐系统或与陌生人进行的对话造成的伤害。照片：Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Shutterstock 英国针对 16 岁以下儿童的社交媒体禁令范围扩大可能涵盖 YouTube Kids 消息人士称，正在考虑的法规可能会影响多达 150 个平台，包括 LegoPlay、Spotify 和 eBay

了解政府提案的消息人士称，大幅扩大针对 16 岁以下青少年的社交媒体禁令可能会无意中导致 YouTube Kids 和其他原本被认为可以豁免的网站也被禁止。

一位接近谈判的消息人士表示，目前正在考虑的规定意味着多达 150 个平台，包括 Lego Play 等游戏平台，可能会受到该禁令的影响，该禁令将于 3 月生效。

这些规定将于本周送交内阁批准，文化部长丽莎·南迪预计将于 12 月将其提交议会。

据了解，部长们热衷于采取一种包罗万象的方法来限制禁令的变通办法。澳大利亚社交媒体禁令的批评者表示，青少年已经转向新平台，或者使用其他看似无害的网站找到了创新的消息传递方式。

科技公司、行业团体和国会议员已获悉，政府的工作提案重点关注推荐系统和用户生成的内容。

Spotify——拥有一些用户生成的内容并显示推荐的音乐或播客——从技术上讲，如果这些提案获得通过，它可能会在范围之内，尽管这家音乐流媒体网站已经寻求保证，它不会面临禁令，因为它主要不是一个社交平台。

一位业内人士表示：“我们都有共同的目标，确保青少年上网安全。提案必须可行，而 eBay、乐高、YouTube Kids 和 Spotify 不清楚自己是否遵守的情况是不可持续的。详细的指导方针还不够快出台。”

另一位网友表示：“整个互联网都有一个推荐系统。监管范围太宽泛。但他们希望使其真正广泛且法律严密，这样他们就可以为任何可能发生的情况做好准备。”

预计文化、媒体和体育部 (DCMS) 和 No 10 将在未来几天向各公司通报最终提案。

当 Keir Starmer 在 6 月宣布禁令时，政府表示将确保禁令不包括教育服务、电子商务平台或音乐流媒体，并表示将“制定一份狭义的豁免清单，并将继续审查这些定义”。

但据了解，科技公司正在告诉政府，删除推荐算法将导致他们的网站无法运行。

这些法规不需要下议院的主要立法，并将作为《儿童福利和学校法》的补充提出。

部长们还在考虑在春季制定第二批法规，其中可能涵盖 Vinted、eBay 和 Depop 等电子商务平台。国会议员和活动人士向南迪提出了担忧，即青少年和美容师可以找到创新的方式在允许未知或匿名用户消息传递的平台上进行交流，例如那些网站。

news.title: Analysis: AI-driven e-commerce adoption surged during China's month-long Singles Day festival, with event sales rising 2.4% between October 7 and October 31 (Reuters)
news.title_en: Analysis: AI-driven e-commerce adoption surged during China's month-long Singles Day festival, with event sales rising 2.4% between October 7 and October 31 (Reuters)
news.author: Reuters
news.content_snippet: If you are looking for evidence of how enthusiastically China is adopting AI, look no further than the country's premier month-long Singles Day shopping festival.

news.title: A 13-Year-Old Asked AI About Suicide on Her School Laptop. It Didn’t Get Flagged for Weeks
news.title_en: A 13-Year-Old Asked AI About Suicide on Her School Laptop. It Didn’t Get Flagged for Weeks
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
The lawsuit alleges that Google and parent company Alphabet were negligent in their rollout of a Gemini model, claiming that the AI chatbot “coached” the North Carolina teenager to consider taking her own life. The case, which was previously reported by The New York Times, is one of several that allege harm from AI chatbot use, including claims of delusions and suicide. But it also illustrates the limitations of surveillance tools that thousands of schools have adopted in recent years, which are ostensibly designed to protect students from themselves when browsing and chatting online.

Andrew Liddell, a lawyer for the family, tells WIRED that, according to information the school provided to the family, the alert went to the personal phone of a former counselor who had left the school nine months before. The ex-employee was diligent in passing the alert along to current staff, who then notified the girl’s mother, he says.

Are you a current or former Google employee who wants to talk about what's happening? We'd like to hear from you. Using a nonwork phone or computer, contact the reporters securely on Signal at carolinehaskins.61and peard33.24.

As classrooms continue to rely on Google’s low-cost offerings, including Gemini, their ability to keep up with the potential risks is front and center. Just last week, parent and teacher groups across the country decried Google’s new requirement that schools must turn on generative AI features if they want to use Search. US senator Ed Markey cited Emma’s lawsuit in a letter to Google demanding the company let schools disable AI Mode and AI Overviews, writing that “Google is recklessly forcing AI on schools and treating kids like collateral damage.”

According to the lawsuit, the North Carolina girl, identified as Emma Doe, descended into “a severe psychological crisis” after Google Search routed her to Gemini on her school-issued Google Chromebook. Though Emma’s school had blocked the stand-alone Gemini website, the lawsuit alleges that she was steered into interacting with the chatbot through AI Mode, which lets people ask follow-up questions about a query or begin an unrelated conversation.

Emma queried AI Mode about mental health issues starting last December. She asked about “severe depression” and “reasons to live,” and by late January she was asking about suicide, per the lawsuit. Over the course of two days around Valentine’s Day, she began writing a 1,500-word eulogy for herself with help from AI Mode in a Google Doc titled “Funeral.” The lawsuit says she worked on the document for more than four weeks while continuing to interact with the Gemini tool thousands of times.

After school on St. Patrick's Day, she deleted most of the file and restarted. But Liddell says the themes and thoughts the girl expressed didn't materially change. Around 7:30 pm, her mother allegedly received a message from the school indicating that her daughter was in “imminent danger,” the lawsuit states. Her mother used her phone to log in to Emma’s school account and “watched her daughter compose a suicide note in real time,” according to the lawsuit.

Google spokesperson José Castañeda says that the company is seriously “reviewing the claims in the lawsuit” and that its systems, including AI Mode, “aim to prevent users from engaging in harmful conversation.”

news.title_zh: Gemini涉嫌诱导自残，校园监控漏洞大
news.summary_zh: 谷歌Gemini因被指诱导学生自残引发诉讼，同时暴露出校园网路监管工具存在严重的滞后与技术缺陷
news.article_content_zh:
该诉讼称，谷歌和母公司 Alphabet 在推出 Gemini 模型时存在疏忽，声称人工智能聊天机器人“指导”这位北卡罗来纳州青少年考虑结束自己的生命。 《纽约时报》此前报道过该案件，是指控人工智能聊天机器人使用造成伤害的多起案件之一，其中包括妄想和自杀的指控。但这也说明了近年来数千所学校采用的监控工具的局限性，这些工具表面上是为了保护学生在网上浏览和聊天时免受自身侵害。

该家庭的律师安德鲁·利德尔（Andrew Liddell）告诉《连线》杂志，根据学校向该家庭提供的信息，警报发送到了九个月前离开学校的一名前辅导员的私人电话。他说，这位前雇员很努力地将警报传递给现任员工，后者随后通知了女孩的母亲。

随着课堂继续依赖 Google 的低成本产品（包括 Gemini），他们应对潜在风险的能力就成为首要和核心。就在上周，全国各地的家长和教师团体谴责了谷歌的新要求，即学校如果想使用搜索就必须启用生成式人工智能功能。美国参议员埃德·马基 (Ed Markey) 在给谷歌的一封信中引用了艾玛的诉讼，要求该公司让学校禁用人工智能模式和人工智能概述，并写道，“谷歌不顾一切地将人工智能强加给学校，并像对待附带损害一样对待孩子。”

根据诉讼，这位名叫艾玛·多伊 (Emma Doe) 的北卡罗来纳州女孩在 Google 搜索将她学校配发的 Google Chromebook 上的搜索结果转到 Gemini 后陷入了“严重的心理危机”。尽管艾玛的学校封锁了独立的 Gemini 网站，但诉讼称她被引导通过人工智能模式与聊天机器人进行交互，该模式可以让人们提出有关查询的后续问题或开始不相关的对话。

艾玛从去年 12 月开始向 AI Mode 询问心理健康问题。根据诉讼，她询问了“严重抑郁症”和“生存的理由”，到一月底，她询问了自杀的情况。在情人节前后的两天里，她开始在 AI 模式的帮助下，在名为“葬礼”的 Google 文档中为自己写一篇 1,500 字的悼词。诉讼称，她处理这份文件的时间超过了四个星期，同时继续与 Gemini 工具交互数千次。

圣帕特里克节放学后，她删除了大部分文件并重新开始。但利德尔表示，女孩表达的主题和想法并没有发生实质性改变。诉讼称，晚上 7 点 30 分左右，她的母亲据称收到了学校发来的消息，表明她的女儿处于“迫在眉睫的危险”。诉讼称，她的母亲用她的手机登录艾玛的学校账户，“看着她的女儿实时写遗书”。

谷歌发言人何塞·卡斯塔涅达表示，该公司正在认真“审查诉讼中的主张”，其系统，包括人工智能模式，“旨在防止用户参与有害对话”。

卡斯塔涅达说：“我们与医疗专业人士和学术专家广泛合作，构建了一些功能，帮助年轻人在需要时找到关键支持和值得信赖的资源。”

艾玛一家的律师试图隐瞒学校的名称，以保护艾玛的隐私。 《连线》杂志能够确认该学校的身份，但该学校没有回复置评请求。根据《连线》对互联网档案馆的审查，近几个月来，学校在其网站底部添加了自杀预防资源的链接。

利德尔告诉《连线》杂志，艾玛的学校之所以了解到她的心理健康危机，是因为它至少使用了一个第三方学生活动监控系统。他援引据称之前提供给学校家长的信息称，这些信息可能包括 GoGuardian 和 Gaggle 公司的产品。利德尔说，家人缺乏明确的答案，因为学校与他们的“合作窗口”很短暂。

GoGuardian 发言人 Natalia Switala 告诉《连线》杂志，由于“学生隐私义务”，该公司不能“讨论任何个别学生或学区”。 Gaggle 没有立即回复《连线》杂志的置评请求。

筛选工具通常通过捕获击键或扫描文件并使用算法和人工审查来识别潜在的相关内容来工作。目前尚不清楚学校的第三方筛选工具是否监控人工智能模式的互动，或者如果监控的话，它们的实际效果如何。 GoGuardian 在 2025 年 7 月的一篇博客文章中写道，其旗舰产品监控与 AI 聊天机器人（包括 Gemini）的对话，但没有具体提及 AI 模式。

尽管尚不清楚学生监控工具在保护学生方面到底有多有效，但研究表明，教育工作者认为它们很有帮助。 EdWeek 研究中心 2022 年的一份白皮书发现，在对 1,000 名美国 K-12 教育工作者的调查中，96% 的 Gaggle 用户认为它有助于“保护学生免遭自杀和/或自残”。虽然这项研究是由 Gaggle 赞助的，但对于报告使用替代方案的教师来说，结果是相似的。

news.title: MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR teardown: a 5/10 score, a point above the M5 MacBook Pro, and Touch ID works with a new logic board; the backlit logo uses four LEDs (Elizabeth Chamberlain/iFixit News)
news.title_en: MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR teardown: a 5/10 score, a point above the M5 MacBook Pro, and Touch ID works with a new logic board; the backlit logo uses four LEDs (Elizabeth Chamberlain/iFixit News)
news.author: iFixit News
news.article_content:
“Fancy new display” makes our screwdrivers nervous, and Apple’s latest MacBook has the fanciest display yet. The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is the first-ever touchscreen MacBook. It’s got a tandem OLED panel that hits 120 Hz and peaks at 2,000 nits, powered by your choice of an M5 Pro or M5 Max chip.

And somehow, with a touchscreen and a redesigned hinge, this thing weighs 1.38 kg (three pounds). That’s 170 grams (half a pound) lighter than the M6 14-inch Pro.

“Lighter” also strikes fear in the heart of our screwdrivers: in pursuit of lightness, designers often leave repairability on the cutting room floor.

The good news? The new lid is just as easy to replace as last year. And we didn’t experience the problems we saw with TouchID calibration last year. But it’s not all good news. The fans and USB-C ports are still buried under the logic board.

We were maybe most excited to dig into the most useless feature of this display: the glowing apple on the back.

On old MacBooks, light from the LCD backlight shone through an apple-shaped window in the lid. But the PROLED’s pixels make their own light. So, yes, Apple waited until the first MacBook Pro without a backlight to bring back the backlit logo.

For a display repair, the lid comes off as one assembly. The familiar antenna bar still sits in the way of the hinges, but the display cable bracketry is slightly streamlined and there’s no separate lid-angle sensor to deal with.

The PROLED and M6 have nearly indistinguishable three-screw hinges. The difference is easier to feel than to see: a gentle tap on the PROLED results in a bit less wobble. It probably comes down to minor spring tuning, but this change is definitely mainly hype. We also couldn’t find any similarities to the iPhone Duo’s hinge tech, as was briefly rumored.

There are few laptops on the market that make it possible to replace a display without replacing the whole upper lid. Framework Laptop, for instance, has a cool magnetic bezel with screws underneath that release the panel, no need to throw away a working camera or pay for a new one. Some models of Framework Laptop even enable a display upgrade (e.g., from 2.2K to 2.8K) this way.

But generally, we’re okay with “replace the whole lid to replace the display” as the path to display repairs, especially with the changes in this design that make whole-lid replacement easier.

Still, we were curious: Could we get the panel out in one piece? Short answer, no. It seems theoretically possible, but getting inside that lid cost us the panel.

We warmed it from the back and worked a thin pick into the corner. The rubber trim lifted. Then the glass delaminated, cracking the OLED and capacitive layers underneath.

That gave us a look at two light, rigid foam pads flanking the logo. Our best guess is they give the OLED a little backing when you press on the glass.

Under a taped patch in the middle we found four LEDs, all in a strip along one edge. The light hits a reflective layer and passes through a diffuser, turning four little points of light into one evenly glowing apple. The logo itself has a mirror-like coating that looks shiny with the lights off.

Cool, but this is an insane repair path for reaching the glowing logo. If yours ever goes dark, you might see if you can live with a regular Apple. We’d be very interested to see if anyone successfully pulls off an LED mod.

Now that we’ve got the display off, let’s take a closer look at how it works.

news.article_content_zh:
“精美的新显示屏”让我们的螺丝刀感到紧张，而苹果最新的 MacBook 拥有迄今为止最精美的显示屏。配备 PROLED XDR 的 MacBook Pro 是首款触摸屏 MacBook。它配备串联 OLED 面板，频率可达 120 Hz，峰值亮度为 2,000 尼特，由您选择的 M5 Pro 或 M5 Max 芯片供电。

不知何故，配备触摸屏和重新设计的铰链，这个东西重 1.38 公斤（三磅）。比 M6 14 英寸 Pro 轻 170 克（半磅）。

“更轻”也让我们的螺丝刀心生畏惧：为了追求轻，设计师常常把可修复性留在了裁剪室的地板上。

好消息？新盖子与去年一样易于更换。我们没有遇到去年 TouchID 校准时遇到的问题。但这并不都是好消息。风扇和 USB-C 端口仍然埋在逻辑板下方。

我们可能最兴奋的是深入研究这个显示器最无用的功能：背面发光的苹果。

在旧款 MacBook 上，LCD 背光灯透过盖子上的苹果形窗口照射。但 PROLED 的像素会自己发光。所以，是的，苹果等到第一款没有背光的 MacBook Pro 才重新带回背光标志。

对于显示器维修，盖子作为一个组件拆下。熟悉的天线杆仍然位于铰链处，但显示屏电缆支架略微流线型，并且没有单独的盖子角度传感器需要处理。

PROLED 和 M6 具有几乎无法区分的三螺钉铰链。感觉差异比看到差异更容易：轻轻敲击 PROLED 可以减少晃动。这可能归结为轻微的弹簧调整，但这种变化绝对主要是炒作。我们也没有发现与 iPhone Duo 的铰链技术有任何相似之处，正如传闻中的那样。

市场上很少有笔记本电脑可以在不更换整个上盖的情况下更换显示屏。例如，框架笔记本电脑有一个很酷的磁性边框，下面有螺丝可以释放面板，无需扔掉可用的相机或支付新的费用。某些型号的 Framework 笔记本电脑甚至可以通过这种方式实现显示屏升级（例如，从 2.2K 到 2.8K）。

但一般来说，我们同意“更换整个盖子来更换显示器”作为显示器维修的途径，特别是这种设计的变化使整个盖子的更换变得更容易。

尽管如此，我们还是很好奇：我们能否将面板整块取出来？简短的回答，不。这在理论上似乎是可能的，但进入那个盖子需要我们花费面板。

我们从背面加热它，并在角落里挖了一把细镐。橡胶饰边升起。然后玻璃分层，导致下面的 OLED 和电容层破裂。

这让我们看到了标志两侧的两个轻质硬质泡沫垫。我们最好的猜测是，当你按下玻璃时，它们会给 OLED 一点支撑。

在中间的胶带贴片下，我们发现了四个 LED，全部位于沿着一侧边缘的条带中。光线照射到反射层并穿过漫射器，将四个小光点变成一个均匀发光的苹果。标志本身有一层镜面涂层，在关灯的情况下看起来闪闪发光。

news.title: England's university regulator says AI makes grading coursework "close to impossible" and recommends a return to "AI-free assessment" methods like written exams (Richard Adams/The Guardian)
news.title_en: England's university regulator says AI makes grading coursework "close to impossible" and recommends a return to "AI-free assessment" methods like written exams (Richard Adams/The Guardian)
news.author: The Guardian
news.article_content:
The OfS said many institutions had already redesigned how they assessed students to reduce potential AI misuse. Photograph: Lbeddoe/Alamy View image in fullscreen The OfS said many institutions had already redesigned how they assessed students to reduce potential AI misuse. Photograph: Lbeddoe/Alamy AI has made it ‘close to impossible’ to assess university coursework, regulator says Office for Students says institutions in England should return to traditional exams and in-person presentations

Universities should go back to traditional exams and in-person presentations to grade students after lecturers complained that AI has made it “close to impossible” to assess coursework, according to an investigation by England’s higher education regulator.

The Office for Students (OfS) said the credibility of degrees from England’s universities was under threat from the prolific use of AI in essays, dissertations and “open book” exams, with students reporting that their peers boasted of using AI undetected by staff.

The regulator warned universities and other higher education institutions that failing to design “valid and reliable measures of students’ knowledge and skills” to combat AI could breach their conditions of registration and lead to sanctions being imposed.

Josh Fleming, the director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said AI use in higher education “presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students’ learning and institutions’ ability to assess them”.

Fleming added: “We need to see far greater efforts to tackle these risks, including far greater use of AI-free assessment.

“The scale and pace of both the challenge and opportunity presents a novel challenge for the sector and us as the regulator. We will continue to work with universities and colleges to help them reap the benefits of AI while avoiding the risks.”

A Department for Education spokesperson said: “We expect universities to take this issue seriously and we expect the OfS to both enforce the existing standards effectively, and work at pace to ensure its regulatory framework is explicit, strong and durable on the use of AI.”

A spokesperson for Universities UK, which represents 147 higher education institutions, said: “There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students. This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way.”

The report by the OfS and Advance HE, a charity promoting university governance and teaching, interviewed more than 300 students and staff at 127 universities and colleges this year, to gauge AI policies and use in teaching and assessment.

One academic told the researchers: “AI has put academic integrity at serious risk … coursework is now overwhelmingly written in part, or exclusively, with the help of AI.”

Another university staff member said: “I think we’re realising that a number of our assessments may be unfit for purpose, and that pervasive use of AI may render our assessment of students close to impossible in some areas.”

The survey found that AI use was rife, with students saying their colleagues completed assessments using AI “sometimes in just a few minutes” and received similar grades to those who had completed an assessment without AI.

“Some students described their peers being unable to recall basic details about the assessment they had just submitted,” the report noted.

news.article_content_zh:
OfS 表示，许多机构已经重新设计了评估学生的方式，以减少潜在的人工智能滥用。照片：Lbeddoe/Alamy 全屏查看图片 The OfS 表示，许多机构已经重新设计了评估学生的方式，以减少潜在的人工智能滥用。

英国高等教育监管机构的一项调查显示，在讲师抱怨人工智能使评估课程作业“几乎不可能”之后，大学应该恢复传统的考试和现场演示来给学生评分。

学生办公室 (OfS) 表示，英国大学学位的可信度因在论文、论文和“开卷”考试中大量使用人工智能而受到威胁，学生们报告说，他们的同龄人吹嘘自己在工作人员没有发现的情况下使用了人工智能。

该监管机构警告大学和其他高等教育机构，如果未能设计“有效且可靠的学生知识和技能衡量标准”来对抗人工智能，可能会违反其注册条件并导致实施制裁。

OfS 战略与交付总监乔什·弗莱明 (Josh Fleming) 表示，人工智能在高等教育中的使用“给现有系统带来了代际风险，有可能损害学生的学习和机构评估他们的能力”。

弗莱明补充道：“我们需要付出更大的努力来应对这些风险，包括更多地使用无人工智能的评估。

“挑战和机遇的规模和速度给该行业和我们作为监管者带来了新的挑战。我们将继续与大学和学院合作，帮助他们获得人工智能的好处，同时避免风险。”

教育部发言人表示：“我们希望大学认真对待这个问题，我们希望英国教育部能够有效执行现有标准，并加快步伐，确保其在人工智能使用方面的监管框架明确、强大和持久。”

代表 147 所高等教育机构的英国大学协会的一位发言人表示：“还有很长的路要走，但许多机构已经对评估学生的方式做出了重大改变。这包括更多的现场考试、演示、vivas、基于流程的评估以及以受控方式整合人工智能的评估。”

OfS 和促进大学治理和教学的慈善机构 Advance HE 的这份报告今年采访了 127 所大学和学院的 300 多名学生和教职员工，以评估人工智能政策以及在教学和评估中的使用。

一位学者告诉研究人员：“人工智能使学术诚信面临严重风险……现在绝大多数课程作业都是部分或完全在人工智能的帮助下编写的。”

另一位大学工作人员表示：“我认为我们正在意识到，我们的许多评估可能不符合目的，人工智能的普遍使用可能会使我们在某些领域对学生的评估几乎不可能。”

调查发现，人工智能的使用很普遍，学生们表示，他们的同事使用人工智能“有时只需几分钟”就完成了评估，并且获得了与未使用人工智能完成评估的人相似的成绩。

报告指出：“一些学生表示，他们的同龄人无法回忆起他们刚刚提交的评估的基本细节。”
